subject: DAY-TO-YYYYDDD function
notes: The same sentence as §15.23.3 r5, tested the same way in the same program's DAY-* lines: the substituted value staged through an integer item (§8.4.3.2.3 SR11 bars writing NUMVAL in argument-3), argument-1 derived from the execution year (YY = MOD(CY,100), argument-1 = YY*1000+365), and the omitted-vs-explicit identity asserted at argument-2 = 0 and -1 so a one-year skew in either direction breaks it. Clock-free witnesses: nnn = 365 by §15.25.4 r1, and two explicit argument-3 values that must differ (1885365 / 1985365). The DayToYyyyddd 2-argument overload IS the mechanism r5 names — it supplies RunUnit.Current.Clock.Now().Year — and is added to the code-location for that reason.
